meta.label: Laundry
meta.attribution: Curated from public ingredient disclosures, certifications, brand sustainability pages, and packaging claims - not lab-measured. Plastic-light formats help, but cold washes, full loads, garment care, and avoiding over-washing often matter more than detergent brand. Reviewed 2026-06. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare laundry by environmental impact, disclosure, packaging, and animal-testing evidence.

axes.label: Environmental impact
axes.question: Does lower environmental impact matter more?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Laundry strips (e.g. Tru Earth)

environment.note: Concentrated sheet format reduces liquid weight and jug waste, but Tru Earth lists polyvinyl alcohol in its detergent ingredients.

transparency.note: Tru Earth publishes a laundry detergent ingredient table with CAS numbers and functions.

packaging.note: Product page states plastic-jug-free, recyclable packaging for laundry strips.

cruelty_free.note: FAQ says the laundry detergent is vegan and not tested on animals by Tru Earth or its ingredient suppliers.

accessibility.note: Sold direct online with subscription/bulk options; still more specialized than supermarket liquid detergents.

products.description: Ultra-light detergent sheets reduce jug waste and shipping weight, though some sheets still use PVA film-forming chemistry.

products.name: Soap nuts / soapberries

environment.note: Ecozone describes soap nuts as 100% plant-based/all-natural and reusable for multiple washes.

transparency.note: Single-ingredient dried soap nuts make the formula easy to understand; effectiveness depends on water and laundry conditions.

packaging.note: Ecozone sells a 300g cotton bag intended for up to 100 washes.

cruelty_free.note: A whole plant-shell product rather than an animal-derived detergent; certification varies by seller.

accessibility.note: Niche product that requires a different routine and is easier to find online/zero-waste retail than mainstream stores.

products.description: Dried soapberry shells are a one-ingredient laundry option with very low packaging, but they are niche and less familiar to use.

products.name: Meliora Laundry Powder
products.description: A concentrated laundry powder with fully disclosed ingredients, MADE SAFE certification, and low-waste packaging.

environment.note: Laundry powder is MADE SAFE-certified and concentrated, with safer-ingredient screening for people and ecosystems.

transparency.note: Meliora says every ingredient is listed on labels and online, with a short laundry ingredient list.

packaging.note: Media kit says the product line is single-use plastic-free with refills and zero-waste bucket options.

cruelty_free.note: Leaping Bunny lists Meliora Cleaning Products as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Sold direct online and through zero-waste/natural retailers; less mainstream than grocery brands.

products.name: Blueland Laundry Tablets
products.description: A tablet detergent system built to avoid plastic jugs and pod film while carrying multiple third-party certifications.

environment.note: Laundry tablets are EWG Verified and certified/recognized through C2C Material Health, USDA BioPreferred, and other programs.

transparency.note: Blueland help page points users to published ingredient lists for products.

packaging.note: Laundry tablet starter/refill page says tablets are 100% plastic-free, PVA-free, and use compostable refill packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Blueland states Leaping Bunny certification applies to all products.

accessibility.note: Sold direct with autoship and refill pricing; retail availability is growing but still mostly premium.

products.name: Bio-D

environment.note: Bio-D describes its range as naturally derived, biodegradable, made with solar energy, and refill-friendly.

transparency.note: Bio-D publishes product and ingredient information for its laundry range.

packaging.note: Bio-D highlights refill sizes, closed-loop larger containers, and 100% recycled plastic bottles.

cruelty_free.note: Bio-D states products are vegan and cruelty-free with Vegan Society/Cruelty Free International signals.

accessibility.note: Strongest in UK/EU through stockists and refill shops; less available globally.

products.description: A UK eco-cleaning brand with vegan/cruelty-free credentials, refill options, and recycled plastic packaging.

products.name: Dropps

environment.note: Dropps reports ultra-concentrated formulas, USDA Certified Biobased formulations, water savings, and lower shipping impacts.

transparency.note: EWG product page shows good ingredient disclosure, while also naming PVOH film and moderate-concern ingredients.

packaging.note: Dropps says it shifted detergent pods to recyclable paperboard packaging; pod film is still PVOH.

cruelty_free.note: Dropps says its cruelty-free products are Leaping Bunny Certified.

accessibility.note: Direct/subscription model with broader retail launch noted in 2024, but not as ubiquitous as mainstream brands.

products.description: Concentrated laundry pods in recyclable paperboard packaging, with good certifications but a PVOH pod-film caveat.

products.name: Attitude

environment.note: Laundry detergent page describes plant/mineral-based, vegan formula effective in cold water and sold in eco-refill sizes.

transparency.note: EWG listing says the product bears the EWG Verified mark and provides full ingredient transparency, including fragrance.

packaging.note: ATTITUDE laundry page offers 4L eco-refill formats, though liquid formats still involve packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Laundry page says the vegan formula is PETA-certified.

accessibility.note: Available online and through some retail channels, but pricier and less universal than mainstream detergents.

products.description: An EWG Verified, vegan liquid detergent line with refill sizes and comparatively strong ingredient-safety signals.

products.name: AspenClean Laundry Detergent
products.description: A certification-heavy unscented liquid detergent with EWG Verified, ECOCERT, vegan and Leaping Bunny signals, but still a bottled liquid.

environment.note: Unscented detergent is EWG Verified, ECOCERT certified, plant/mineral-based, and made without phosphates, petroleum and synthetic fragrance.

transparency.note: Product page discloses the full ingredient list and says all ingredients are disclosed.

packaging.note: AspenClean says packaging uses post-consumer resin, but the unscented detergent remains a liquid bottle rather than a plastic-free format.

cruelty_free.note: Certifications page and product page state vegan and cruelty-free status with Leaping Bunny certification.

accessibility.note: Sold direct online in the US/Canada with premium pricing and free-shipping thresholds, so access is narrower than supermarket detergents.

products.name: Dirty Labs Bio Laundry Detergent
products.description: A hyper-concentrated enzyme liquid in recyclable aluminum packaging, with strong ingredient-safety certifications.

environment.note: Free & Clear detergent is EPA Safer Choice, USDA Biobased, biodegradable, and optimized for cold water.

transparency.note: FAQ says detergents carry EPA Safer Choice/USDA Biobased, Free & Clear is EWG Verified, and certification details are public.

packaging.note: Product page says the bottle is recyclable aluminum and the formula is hyper-concentrated.

cruelty_free.note: FAQ says products are PETA-certified vegan and animal test-free.

accessibility.note: US direct/retail availability with premium pricing; concentrated refills improve per-load economics.

products.name: Molly's Suds
products.description: A widely available cleaner-ingredient laundry powder with Leaping Bunny certification and EWG-rated formulas.

environment.note: Original Laundry Powder uses a simple powder formula and is rated A by EWG, but it is not EWG Verified.

transparency.note: Mollys Suds publishes ingredient information and notes the Original Laundry Powder EWG rating publicly.

packaging.note: Powder format avoids water-heavy jugs but is commonly sold in flexible pouches rather than fully plastic-free packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Leaping Bunny features Mollys Suds laundry care as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Widely available in US online and big-box retail with moderate per-load pricing.

products.name: Nellie's Laundry Soda
products.description: A concentrated four-ingredient powder sold in pouches, tins, and bulk buckets, strongest for low-water formula and reusable packaging.

environment.note: Laundry Soda is a highly concentrated four-ingredient powder that dissolves in cold or hot water and is septic safe.

transparency.note: Product and FAQ pages disclose the simple Laundry Soda formula and note the plant-based surfactant source.

packaging.note: Sold in pouch, reusable tin, and larger bucket formats, reducing reliance on water-heavy plastic liquid jugs.

cruelty_free.note: FAQ says Nellie's products are Leaping Bunny Certified with no animal testing.

accessibility.note: Product page lists multiple sizes and roughly $0.28 per load, with broad online retail availability.

products.name: ECOS Laundry Detergent

environment.note: ECOS Free & Clear liquid detergent is EPA Safer Choice-certified and uses plant-derived surfactants.

transparency.note: ECOS publishes full ingredient lists for laundry products, including CAS/function details on Safer Choice listings.

packaging.note: Liquid format remains plastic-bottle based, so packaging is weaker than tablets/sheets despite broader company sustainability work.

cruelty_free.note: Leaping Bunny lists ECOS as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: ECOS is sold through major retailers and online, with lower per-load pricing than many boutique low-waste detergents.

products.description: A widely available Safer Choice liquid detergent: better ingredients and cruelty-free certification, but still a plastic-bottle product.

products.name: Earth Breeze

environment.note: Sheet format avoids bulky liquid jugs and uses compact detergent, but ingredient disclosure includes polyvinyl alcohol.

transparency.note: Earth Breeze publishes ingredient lists for fragrance-free and scented laundry sheets in its help center.

packaging.note: Product page frames the sheets as eliminating plastic jugs and using slim cardboard packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Earth Breeze product page states the laundry sheets are cruelty-free and vegan.

accessibility.note: Sold direct and increasingly through major retail marketplaces, with simple subscription-style pricing.

products.description: A popular detergent-sheet option with very low packaging bulk, scored with a PVA/ingredient-transparency caveat.

products.name: Kind Laundry

environment.note: Kind Laundry detergent sheets are USDA BioPreferred and use plant-derived ingredients, according to brand and EWG listings.

transparency.note: EWG lists Kind Laundry Fragrance Free sheets as EWG Verified with full ingredient transparency.

packaging.note: Brand positions the sheets around zero-waste/plastic-free packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Leaping Bunny lists Kind Laundry as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Mostly direct and online marketplace availability, with higher per-load pricing than mainstream liquids.

products.description: A premium detergent-sheet brand with stronger third-party signals than many sheet competitors.

products.name: Cleancult Laundry

environment.note: Concentrated laundry refill lists a plant-derived/surfactant enzyme formula and avoids several common harsh additives.

transparency.note: Product page publishes the full ingredient list for the fragrance-free liquid laundry refill.

packaging.note: Cleancult says laundry refills use paper-based, 100% recyclable packaging instead of conventional plastic jugs.

cruelty_free.note: Leaping Bunny lists Cleancult as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Available through Cleancult and large US retailers, but refills are still pricier than conventional jugs.

products.description: A lower-plastic laundry refill route in paper-based cartons, with Leaping Bunny certification and growing retail reach.

products.name: Common Good Laundry Refill Box
products.description: A large-format enzyme laundry refill box designed to bring a refill station home and cut bottle waste.

environment.note: Refill box is 3x concentrated, plant-based, enzyme-powered, biodegradable, septic/greywater safe, and rated for 480 HE loads.

transparency.note: Product page publishes full ingredients for the laundry refill box.

packaging.note: Common Good says the refill box uses 86% less plastic, PCR cardboard, a reusable spigot, and a liner return/closed-loop program.

cruelty_free.note: Product details state the formula is vegan and cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: The refill box lowers per-load cost to about $0.35 but requires a large upfront purchase and direct shipping.

products.name: Smol

environment.note: Smol says concentrated formulas cut carbon/packaging and omit phosphates, animal fats, and harsh preservatives.

transparency.note: Smol ingredient article points users to product ingredient lists and explains ingredient choices.

packaging.note: Laundry capsule help page says plan/trial packs use 100% plastic-free packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Smol states all products are vegan and cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Subscription model is convenient in the UK but region-limited compared with global supermarket brands.

products.description: A UK refill-by-mail laundry subscription with concentrated formulas, plastic-free capsule packs, and vegan/cruelty-free claims.

products.name: Ecover

environment.note: Ecover says it prioritizes plant-derived, biodegradable ingredients where possible.

transparency.note: Product pages disclose plant-based/biodegradable ingredient positioning and usage details by item.

packaging.note: Laundry liquid page lists 100% post-consumer recycled plastic bottle and refill guidance.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Ecover (SC Johnson) as cruelty-free; parent-company debates remain for stricter shoppers.

accessibility.note: Widely sold in UK/EU supermarkets and refill shops, with some international availability.

products.description: A widely available plant-based laundry brand with refill/recycled-plastic packaging, tempered by SC Johnson parent-company concerns.

products.name: Seventh Generation
products.description: A broadly available laundry brand with strong ingredient/transparency signals and mainstream retail access.

environment.note: Free & Clear detergent is plant-based and USDA Certified Biobased 97%; brand also has B Corp certification.

transparency.note: Seventh Generation maintains an ingredient glossary and frames ingredient disclosure as a right-to-know policy.

packaging.note: Brand reports broad PCR/recyclability goals and zero-plastic laundry innovations, but mainstream liquid bottles still use plastic.

cruelty_free.note: Leaping Bunny lists Seventh Generation and the brand says it joined the Leaping Bunny program in 1999.

accessibility.note: Common in US grocery and big-box retail, with online availability and mainstream price/availability advantages.

products.name: Method laundry detergent
products.description: A broadly available concentrated laundry liquid with cruelty-free positioning and high-recycled-content plastic packaging, but still a liquid bottle format.

environment.note: Method's laundry page describes a concentrated formula, and the brand frames its sustainability work around circular packaging and lower-waste design.

transparency.note: Product pages publish ingredient and product-attribute details, with the brand also maintaining an FAQ on vegan and cruelty-free claims.

packaging.note: The Free + Clear laundry bottle is listed as 100% recycled plastic except the lid; Method's sustainability page also highlights recycled recovered coastal plastic work.

cruelty_free.note: Method says its products are cruelty-free, and its sustainability page names Leaping Bunny certification against animal cruelty.

accessibility.note: Sold through Method's online store and many mainstream retailers, though usually at a premium over budget detergents.

products.name: Mrs. Meyer's Clean Day
products.description: A widely stocked scented laundry line with Leaping Bunny certification and plant-derived positioning, tempered by conventional liquid packaging.

environment.note: Product pages describe plant-derived ingredients and stain-fighting enzymes, but the brand remains a scented liquid-detergent line.

transparency.note: Laundry product pages disclose ingredients and formula claims, though fragrance-forward products may still be less ideal for fragrance-sensitive shoppers.

packaging.note: The core laundry line is still sold in conventional bottles, so packaging is materially weaker than sheets, powders, tablets, or refill systems.

cruelty_free.note: Mrs. Meyer's says its formulas are cruelty-free, tested by people and Leaping Bunny certified.

accessibility.note: Commonly available in US grocery, big-box, and online channels, with prices above budget but below many boutique low-waste options.

products.name: Grove Co. laundry
products.description: A mission-driven home-care retailer's laundry line with cold-wash, sheet, refill and plastic-reduction signals, but more limited mainstream access.

environment.note: Grove's cold-wash detergent is described as 96% plant-based and EPA Safer Choice recognized, with cold-water washing framed as an energy-saving design choice.

transparency.note: The product page lists detailed ingredients, banned-ingredient standards and EPA Safer Choice context; Grove also publishes sustainability reports.

packaging.note: Grove's 2025 report says laundry detergent moved to FSC-certified paperboard gabletop refill cartons and tracks lower plastic intensity.

cruelty_free.note: Grove says every product available from Grove is cruelty-free, with Grove-brand formulated products Leaping Bunny approved.

accessibility.note: Mostly online/subscription-led availability and mid-price positioning make it less accessible than supermarket detergents.

products.name: 9 Elements
products.description: A P&G laundry line built around vinegar-powered, limited-ingredient formulas and EPA Safer Choice certification, but still sold in plastic bottles.

environment.note: The unscented detergent page says the formula has nine ingredients or fewer and is EPA Safer Choice certified.

transparency.note: 9 Elements publishes the ingredient list on product pages and SmartLabel lists detailed formula ingredients.

packaging.note: The detergent is a conventional liquid bottle, so packaging does not match sheets, powders, tablets or refill formats.

cruelty_free.note: Parent P&G says it no longer animal-tests consumer products unless required by law and has some certified brands; 9 Elements is not scored as a certified cruelty-free detergent.

accessibility.note: Available through mainstream US retailers and online, but not as ubiquitous as Tide, Gain, or Arm & Hammer.

products.name: Biokleen
products.description: A plant-based, concentrated detergent option with Safer Choice and cruelty-free signals, though still often packaged as liquid detergent.

environment.note: Retail and PETA profiles describe Free & Clear as plant-derived, hypoallergenic and Safer Choice certified.

transparency.note: Retail listings disclose a concentrated Free & Clear formula with no dyes, fragrance or brighteners and note Safer Choice status.

packaging.note: The liquid formula is concentrated, reducing dose and shipment volume, but it remains a plastic-bottle detergent rather than plastic-free packaging.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Biokleen as cruelty-free and says ingredients, finished products, suppliers and third parties follow that standard.

accessibility.note: Sold through online, supermarket, drugstore and health-food channels, but less common than the largest mainstream detergents.

products.name: Ariel
products.description: A major P&G detergent brand with strong cold-wash messaging and broad availability, but conventional formula and packaging tradeoffs.

environment.note: Ariel emphasizes cold-wash carbon savings and material goals, but remains a conventional high-volume detergent brand.

transparency.note: Ariel publishes ingredient explainers and SmartLabel pages disclose ingredients for some P&G Ariel products.

packaging.note: Ariel says packaging is recyclable and participates in P&G fabric-care packaging reduction goals, but plastic and pod formats remain central.

cruelty_free.note: P&G says it no longer animal-tests consumer products unless required by law and has some certified brands; Ariel is not scored as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Ariel is a mass-market detergent brand with broad UK, EU and international retail availability.

products.name: all Free Clear

environment.note: all Free Clear is fragrance/dye-free for sensitive skin, but remains a conventional liquid detergent in plastic packaging.

transparency.note: Brand product page links to SmartLabel, and SmartLabel provides detailed ingredient disclosure.

packaging.note: Baseline product remains a conventional plastic detergent bottle, with no plastic-free packaging claim.

cruelty_free.note: Henkel says animal testing can still be legally required for detergents/cleaning products in some cases, so all is not scored as certified cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Very widely sold mainstream detergent, often recommended for sensitive skin and available in large retail formats.

products.description: A practical sensitive-skin supermarket default, better on fragrance/dye avoidance than on packaging or animal-testing signals.

products.name: Arm & Hammer

environment.note: Clean & Simple is marketed as a shorter-ingredient mainstream formula, but still conventional liquid detergent.

transparency.note: Church & Dwight publishes product ingredient disclosure for Arm & Hammer laundry detergents.

packaging.note: Arm & Hammer says liquid laundry bottles are recyclable #2 plastic; this is recyclable, not plastic-free.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Arm & Hammer / Church & Dwight as not cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Budget-oriented detergent with very broad US retail availability and low-friction use.

products.description: A common budget detergent with better ingredient disclosure than many cheap products, but conventional packaging and weak cruelty-free evidence.

products.name: Persil / OMO

environment.note: Persil is a conventional high-performance detergent; Henkel cites newer concentration improvements rather than a low-impact formula standard.

transparency.note: Henkel SmartLabel pages disclose ingredient lists for US Persil products.

packaging.note: Persil US says packaging is recyclable and liquid bottles/tubs contain up to 50% post-consumer recycled material.

cruelty_free.note: Not a Leaping Bunny/PETA-certified cruelty-free brand; parent and market structure differ by region.

accessibility.note: Mass-market detergent sold through major retailers in many regions.

products.description: A mainstream high-performance detergent family with better recent packaging steps, but limited values certifications and mixed ownership by market.

products.name: Tide (P&G)

environment.note: Tide publishes ingredient lists for conventional liquid/PODS/powder products; no broad low-impact certification for the baseline brand.

transparency.note: P&G/Tide provide ingredient disclosure through Tide ingredient pages and SmartLabel.

packaging.note: Tide says liquid bottles are recyclable and made with at least 25% post-consumer recycled plastic; plastic remains the default format.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Tide (P&G) as not cruelty-free; P&G says it does not animal-test unless required by law.

accessibility.note: Very broad retail availability and low-friction use across regions and machine types.

products.description: The dominant mainstream detergent choice: very accessible and improving some packaging, but still conventional and not cruelty-free certified.

products.name: Gain (P&G)

environment.note: SmartLabel lists a conventional liquid formula with surfactants and fragrance components rather than a cleaner-ingredient certification.

transparency.note: Gain product pages route users to SmartLabel ingredient disclosure, but scent/fragrance complexity remains high.

packaging.note: Baseline Gain remains plastic-bottle/flexible-pod packaging, with some P&G lower-plastic package experiments but no brand-wide plastic-free standard.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Gain (P&G) as not cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Mass-market US detergent sold widely and priced for mainstream accessibility.

products.description: A fragrance-forward mainstream P&G detergent: cheap and available, but with weaker ingredient, packaging, and cruelty-free signals.

products.name: Sheets Laundry Club

environment.note: Concentrated sheets avoid liquid detergent jugs, while the published ingredients still include polyvinyl alcohol.

transparency.note: Sheets Laundry Club publishes detergent-sheet ingredient lists in its help center and on product pages.

packaging.note: The product page highlights sustainable packaging and a sheet format that eliminates liquid-detergent bottle handling.

cruelty_free.note: Sheets Laundry Club says it uses no animal byproducts and does not test ingredients or finished products on animals.

accessibility.note: Sold direct and through major online retail channels at a midrange per-load price.

products.description: A mainstreaming detergent-sheet option with better packaging and cruelty-free signals, but still with the usual PVA caveat.

products.name: Clean People laundry sheets

environment.note: Laundry sheets reduce plastic-jug waste, but EWG lists only partial/generic ingredient disclosure for the fragrance-free sheet product.

transparency.note: EWG rates Clean People sheet ingredient disclosure as poor, so the transparency score stays cautious despite brand claims.

packaging.note: Retail listings describe the sheets as no-plastic-jug detergent in recyclable packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Clean People markets the formula as vegan and cruelty-free, but EWG notes no PETA or Leaping Bunny information.

accessibility.note: Available through Clean People and large retailers such as Walmart, improving access compared with many niche sheet brands.

products.description: A popular sheet detergent with convenient retail access, tempered by weaker independent ingredient-disclosure signals.

products.name: HeySunday laundry detergent sheets

environment.note: HeySunday says its sheets use plant-based, OECD 301b-certified biodegradable ingredients, but the formula includes PVA.

transparency.note: The product page publishes an ingredient panel and identifies PVA; Truth in Advertising has flagged plastic-free/biodegradable claim nuance.

packaging.note: HeySunday says it uses compostable, plastic-free packaging for its laundry sheets.

cruelty_free.note: HeySunday's help center says the laundry sheets are 100% vegan and cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Sold direct with subscription pricing and broad online advertising, but still less accessible than supermarket liquids.

products.description: A heavily marketed sheet detergent with strong packaging claims and vegan/cruelty-free positioning, but some claim nuance around PVA.

products.name: EcoRoots laundry detergent sheets

environment.note: EcoRoots describes its detergent sheets as ultra-concentrated, hypoallergenic, palm-oil-free, and a low-waste alternative to liquids and pods.

transparency.note: The product page lists exclusions and formulation claims, but not a full CAS-style ingredient table for every variant.

packaging.note: EcoRoots says the sheets are packaged in a plastic-free compostable cardboard package.

cruelty_free.note: EcoRoots states the sheets are vegan and cruelty-free on the product page.

accessibility.note: Available direct and through marketplaces, but still a specialty zero-waste-shop product.

products.description: A zero-waste-store sheet detergent with excellent packaging claims, best suited to online buyers already comfortable with sheet formats.

products.name: Force of Nature laundry detergent sheets

environment.note: Force of Nature says all sheet ingredients are biodegradable under OECD 310D and the product is carbon-neutral certified.

transparency.note: The product FAQ lists the full ingredient set and skin-safety testing context.

packaging.note: The brand says the sheets are stored in FSC-certified recyclable paper packaging.

cruelty_free.note: Product page states Leaping Bunny certification and no animal testing by Force of Nature or suppliers.

accessibility.note: Sold direct online; certification depth is strong, but mainstream shelf availability is limited.

products.description: A stronger-evidence sheet option with Leaping Bunny, NEA, carbon-neutral, and full ingredient-list signals.

products.name: Charlie's Soap laundry powder

environment.note: Charlie's Soap laundry powder is described as EPA Safer Choice certified and concentrated at one tablespoon per load.

transparency.note: Retail and EWG listings disclose the core powder ingredients, with EWG rating the laundry powder B.

packaging.note: Powder format avoids shipping mostly water, but public sources do not show a plastic-free packaging standard.

cruelty_free.note: EWG lists animal-testing information as unknown for Charlie's Soap, so the cruelty-free score stays middling.

accessibility.note: Available through major online retailers and some grocery channels at a practical per-load price.

products.description: A practical concentrated powder with Safer Choice and EWG signals, but less clarity on packaging and animal-testing policy.

products.name: Rockin' Green laundry detergent

environment.note: Rockin' Green emphasizes powder formats, plant-based ingredients, biodegradability, and no phosphates or optical brighteners.

transparency.note: The product pages publish formulation-positioning claims, but not a full ingredient disclosure table for every variant.

packaging.note: Powder is concentrated, but public pages do not show plastic-free packaging as a central standard.

cruelty_free.note: Rockin' Green product copy describes its activewear detergent as vegan and cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Sold direct online and through some marketplaces, but mainly a specialty product for cloth diapers/activewear.

products.description: A specialty laundry option for activewear and odor problems, with better formula values than most mainstream liquids but narrower access.

products.name: Zum Clean laundry soap

environment.note: Zum Laundry Soap uses plant-packed ingredients such as saponified coconut oil and baking soda, but remains a liquid product.

transparency.note: Indigo Wild publishes product-ingredient and FAQ pages for Zum product families.

packaging.note: Target lists recycled/recyclable packaging-related claims, but the product is still sold in a conventional liquid bottle.

cruelty_free.note: Indigo Wild says all Zum products are cruelty-free and tested on humans, never animals.

accessibility.note: Available direct and through retailers such as Target and Whole Foods, but at a higher price than budget detergents.

products.description: A scent-forward, plant-based laundry soap with strong cruelty-free language, balanced by liquid-bottle packaging and fragrance sensitivity caveats.

products.name: Purex Free & Clear

environment.note: Free & Clear removes perfume and dyes, but it is still a conventional liquid detergent with mainstream synthetic surfactants.

transparency.note: Henkel SmartLabel and Purex product pages disclose ingredients and sensitive-skin claims.

packaging.note: Purex Free & Clear is sold as conventional liquid detergent in plastic bottles, with no plastic-free format claim.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Purex/Dial as not cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Purex markets Free & Clear as an affordable sensitive-skin detergent with common retail sizes.

products.description: A cheap sensitive-skin mainstream option: useful for access and fragrance avoidance, weak on packaging and cruelty-free values.

products.name: Xtra laundry detergent

environment.note: Xtra FAQ says its liquid cleaning agents are biodegradable, but EWG gives several Xtra laundry products low grades.

transparency.note: Church & Dwight publishes ingredient disclosure forms for Xtra laundry detergent variants.

packaging.note: Xtra is sold as conventional liquid detergent in large plastic bottles rather than plastic-free formats.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Xtra / Church & Dwight as not cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: Xtra FAQ says products are available at most grocery, drug, warehouse, and dollar stores.

products.description: A true value-floor detergent: very available and cheap, but much weaker on formula, packaging, and animal-testing values.

products.name: Woolite Damage Defense

environment.note: Woolite's garment-care premise may help clothes last, but the ingredient disclosure shows a conventional liquid detergent formula.

transparency.note: RB/SmartLabel provides ingredient-level disclosure for Woolite Damage Defense.

packaging.note: Woolite is sold as conventional bottled liquid detergent, not a plastic-free laundry format.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Woolite / Reckitt Benckiser as not cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: A widely distributed specialty detergent for delicates and garment care.

products.description: A mainstream garment-care detergent that may support clothing longevity, but does not solve plastic packaging or cruelty-free concerns.

products.name: Tide evo laundry tiles

environment.note: Tide evo is a 100% concentrated detergent tile designed for cold-water washing, but it is still a P&G mainstream formula.

transparency.note: Tide publishes format claims and comparison pages, but less ingredient detail than dedicated SmartLabel detergent pages.

packaging.note: P&G says Tide evo uses FSC-certified recyclable paper packaging and eliminates the traditional plastic bottle.

cruelty_free.note: PETA lists Tide / P&G as not cruelty-free.

accessibility.note: National-brand rollout and Target listings improve access, though it is newer and pricier than baseline liquids.

products.description: A useful mainstream packaging experiment: better than a jug on format, but still anchored in P&G's broader animal-testing and mass-market tradeoffs.

products.name: Defunkify laundry detergent

environment.note: EPA recognized Defunkify as a Safer Choice formulator and says it had 15 Safer Choice-certified products designed with safer ingredients.

transparency.note: Product pages publish formula claims and ingredients, including a Free & Clear powder ingredient list.

packaging.note: Defunkify sells powder formats and concentrated laundry products, but also liquid detergents in conventional bottles.

products.description: A reusable washer-discharge filter route for households that want capture without disposable filter pods, with installation and cleaning responsibilities.

products.name: Gulp microfibre filter

environment.note: Gulp describes a self-cleaning washing-machine microfibre filter with high claimed capture and no disposable replacement filters.

transparency.note: The product page gives the claimed efficiency, installation route, no-disposable-filter claim, and parent-company identity.

packaging.note: No disposable filter claim is stronger than pod systems, though the device itself is new hardware and not yet universal.

cruelty_free.note: The intervention is mechanical filtration rather than an animal-derived or animal-tested laundry formula.

accessibility.note: Currently most relevant in UK/EU channels and still a specialized add-on rather than a cheap household default.

products.description: A newer self-cleaning microfiber-filter route with strong claimed capture and no disposable filter cartridges, but limited availability and higher setup burden.

products.name: CLEANR washing-machine filter

environment.note: CLEANR says its external washer filter captures over 90% of laundry microplastics before drain release.

transparency.note: CLEANR publishes the capture claim, installation time, app/pod workflow, and maintenance cadence on its product pages.

packaging.note: The system uses refill pods for captured material, which improves containment but creates recurring consumables.

cruelty_free.note: The intervention is hardware filtration rather than animal-derived laundry chemistry.

accessibility.note: The product is simpler than some plumbed filters but still requires upfront cost, installation, pods, and ongoing maintenance.

products.description: A consumer-friendly external microplastic filter with an app and pod workflow: easier to understand than some filters, but less packaging-light than reusable-screen systems.
